title: The 'static lifetime
summary: 'static means "lives for the whole program" - string literals have it for free.
lecture: String literals are baked into the binary, so a &'static str is always valid - the one borrow you can return from a function that takes no inputs, store anywhere, and send across threads without ceremony.

A function returning a reference must tie it to SOMETHING: an input's lifetime, or 'static. With no borrowed inputs, 'static is the only honest option - and only data that truly lives forever qualifies. A local String can't be laundered into 'static by taking a reference to it; it dies at the brace (E0515).
Treat a 'static bound as a strong claim, not a convenience. When the compiler suggests 'static, first ask whether an owned return type is what you actually meant.

example.caption: Literals qualify; locals never do.
